mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% (current level) is associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 returns due to accommodative monetary policy compressing discount rates and supporting equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in <= 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate rising above 0.5% signals monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 8.5% and employment growth (PAYEMS) falls below 132,000 thousand persons, it signals a deteriorating labor market, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to recession fears.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 8.5 AND PAYEMS < 132000, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeds 2% annualized, it signals strong economic demand, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 returns as the economy supports corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in <= 40% of instances where GDPC1_growth > 2% (annualized), or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO below 100) signals weak supply conditions, leading to negative 5-day S&P 500 returns as the market anticipates a slowdown in economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in <= 40% of instances where INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 500 thousand units, it signals weak demand in the housing sector, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to concerns about economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST < 500, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When residential investment (RSAFS) falls below 340,000 million dollars and the federal funds rate remains below 0.5%, it signals a combination of weak demand and accommodative monetary policy, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as the market anticipates a recession despite low rates.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS < 340000 AND FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When annualized inflation (CPIAUCSL growth) exceeds 3%, it signals a high-inflation regime, leading to negative 60-day S&P 500 returns as the market prices in higher interest rates and reduced real returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL_growth > 3% (annualized), or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
